<reason>Elite, razor-close debate. A built the cleaner core mechanism (familiarity over introductions; co-presence as the pre-threshold step; mediation shared through place at one-staff-per-thirty) and a strong under-rebutted hours argument. But B won more of the live clashes: its broad reading of "app-based interventions" survived A's category attack via the symmetry point (rooms need facilitators too); it met A's cost contradiction head-on with amortization and automation-plus-escalation; and its closing directly reversed A's best move, reframing the "pointer" critique as the reason to fund the message, not a second road. A's two clipped rebuttals and phantom reference IDs were real execution costs, and the first clip swallowed A's only mitigation on the homebound — which B's closing converted into a pillar. B's marginal-dollar frame ("don't double what's abundant; buy what's missing") tied its case to the motion's comparative wording more cleanly, giving the slightly clearer voting reason.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>The "expecting them where" sequence: A's Q2 and closing framed B's destination list as proving apps merely point to places, so fund the places. B's closing absorbed and inverted it — the rooms already exist and the lonely walk past them; the scarce ingredient is the expectation ("the message, not the masonry"; when a sign fills an unused road, you fund signs, not a second road). Runner-up: B2.2's symmetry charge, which blunted A's definitional attack by showing both interventions are human-mediated, leaving only the question of which mediation scales.</best_rebuttal>
